# Expert mixing

How a remote-expert pool combines its members at inference. Named by the chosen orchestration profile, not by a flag of its own. Values are zero-argument factories returning a mixer, which reduces stacked expert outputs ``[E, ...]`` to ``[...]``, so a selector can tune a variant without new flags (the same shape as the ``wrappers`` registry).

Namespace: ``registry.namespace("mixing")``, declared in ``praxis.orchestration.mixing`` (6 entries)

## `mean`

Pool average: the consensus, pure bias. Robust and deterministic.

## `sample`

Keep a random half of the experts (at least one), then average. The expected mix is the
mean; the realized mix orbits it, which is the point - exploration off consensus at
inference.

## `sample_quarter`

sample keeping a random quarter of the experts - higher variance.

## `vote`

Average the per-expert distributions (the CALM expert vote): softmax over the last dim,
mean across experts, returned as log-probs so the result stays in logit space.

## `wave`

A standing wave over the expert index weights the pool: expert i gets ``1 +
cos(2*pi*i/E)``, normalized to sum 1, so peers compose by constructive and destructive
interference rather than a flat mean. Deterministic in the peer ordering.

## `wave_high`

wave at doubled frequency over the peer axis.
